documents.title: AI Guidelines
documents.summary: University-wide hub for Mason's AI guidelines: defines generative AI, states guiding principles (human oversight, transparency, compliance, privacy, critical thinking, accuracy, accessibility) and lists uses that violate standing policies. It points to role-based pages and notes that guidance will evolve.
documents.stance_why: The hub sets principles and a list of violations of standing policies, but 'Choose your role below' routes users to role-specific guidance and it sets no default permit or ban for coursework; it urges 'creative and innovative exploration' yet leaves course rules elsewhere, so delegates.

units.why: Frames the whole guideline set as a university framework for 'responsible and ethical use of AI'; it sets purpose and scope, so P56 (institution-wide framework) fits, informs, general.
units.anchor: framework and guidance for the responsible and ethical use of AI across our academic community

units.why: States the documentation 'will continue to evolve' as tools change; a provisional-policy statement, P54 (revisit regularly).
units.anchor: AI guideline documentation will continue to evolve

units.why: Invites instructors to send feedback to the AI Task Force or Stearns Center: a feedback channel, which P54 lists ('feedback is invited'); modality 'may' since it is an invitation.
units.anchor: Instructors are invited to offer feedback or suggest additions

units.why: Defines generative AI as technology and capability, setting what the guidelines cover; P61 (define AI and scope).
units.anchor: Generative AI (GenAI) is a rapidly advancing subfield of AI that is both a technology

units.why: Notes GenAI poses 'challenges around ethics, bias, privacy, security'; a statement naming harms, so P53 fits better than P61 because the point is the concerns, not the definition.
units.anchor: pose challenges around ethics, bias, privacy, security

units.why: Says the university is 'integrating artificial intelligence (AI) capabilities across many of the enterprise applications'; describes institutional provision of AI tools, P17 (sanctioned tools).
units.anchor: the university is integrating artificial intelligence (AI) capabilities across many of the enterprise applications

units.why: Principles are stated to ensure 'responsible, ethical, and effective use' via accountability, transparency, etc.; an institution-wide preamble of principles, P56.
units.anchor: These guiding principles seek to ensure the responsible, ethical, and effective use of AI tools

units.why: 'Humans must remain accountable for all decisions and actions' makes users own outcomes of AI-assisted work. P29 (own what you submit) fits; P31 covers the separate review duty.
units.anchor: Humans must remain accountable for all decisions and actions, even when assisted by AI

units.why: 'Users must review all AI-generated material for accuracy' is a duty to verify output; P31 (verify AI output).
units.anchor: Users must review all AI-generated material for accuracy, reliability, and appropriateness

units.why: 'must maintain the highest standards of transparency ... clearly disclosing when and how AI has been utilized' requires disclosure of AI use in work; P24 (disclose with each submission). Specifics (platform, date) are coded separately as P25.
units.anchor: clearly disclosing when and how AI has been utilized in their work

units.why: Specifies disclosure must identify 'the platform utilized, and the date of use'; citation details, so P25 rather than P24 because it names tool and date.
units.anchor: explicitly identifying AI-generated content, the platform utilized, and the date of use

units.why: 'must follow all relevant laws and university policies regarding copyright, intellectual property' is an IP/compliance duty; P52 (licensing and copyright) is closest, P50 is about personal data.
units.anchor: Users must follow all relevant laws and university policies regarding copyright, intellectual property

units.why: 'Users should protect their personal, confidential information' when using AI tools; data-protection advice, P50.
units.anchor: Users should protect their personal, confidential information and proprietary intellectual property when using AI tools

units.why: AI should be used 'to enhance, not replace, personal reasoning and creativity'; the enhance-not-replace clause makes P32 (student stays primary thinker) the type, though P31 also touches validity.
units.anchor: uses of AI to enhance, not replace, personal reasoning and creativity

units.why: 'Users must cultivate AI literacy by understanding its workings, capabilities, and limitations' is an AI-literacy duty; P44 (teach effective AI use as a skill) is nearest as no literacy type exists.
units.anchor: Users must cultivate AI literacy by understanding its workings, capabilities, and limitations

units.why: 'always verify AI outputs by cross-referencing with reliable sources' and 'responsibility of verifying AI output lies with each user'; P31 verify output.
units.anchor: always verify AI outputs by cross-referencing with reliable sources

units.why: 'Users should ensure that AI tools and instructions are accessible to all members' including people with disabilities; equity and access, P51.
units.anchor: Users should ensure that AI tools and instructions are accessible to all members of our

units.why: 'utilize university-approved platforms and resources' prescribes vetted tools; P50 (prefer university-vetted tools).
units.anchor: utilize university-approved platforms and resources

units.why: 'When in doubt, contact your unit lead before integrating and/or using an AI tool' is an ask-first rule; P10 (when unsure, ask).
units.anchor: When in doubt, contact your unit lead before integrating and/or using an AI tool

units.why: 'Do not enter confidential information ... into publicly available AI tools' forbids pasting protected data into AI; P50 protect personal data, chosen over P20 because it concerns confidential/student/personal data, not assignment specs.
units.anchor: Do not enter confidential information, including proprietary data, student data, personal information

units.why: Warns that free services 'monetize your data'; privacy risk advice, P50.
units.anchor: Free online services typically monetize your data, identity, and how the service is being used

units.why: 'Do not use AI for any activity that could compromise university systems' is a security prohibition; no type covers security misuse, so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: Do not use AI for any activity that could compromise university systems or networks
units.uncovered_note: Prohibition on using AI for hacking, breaching security or exploiting vulnerabilities (security misuse), not about learning or integrity.

units.why: 'Do not use AI to create or distribute malicious content, including malware, viruses, phishing emails' is a harmful-content ban not in any type.
units.anchor: Do not use AI to create or distribute malicious content, including malware, viruses, phishing emails
units.uncovered_note: Prohibition on using AI to create malware, phishing or other harmful content.

units.why: 'Do not use AI to create or distribute content that violates copyright'; copyright/IP rule, P52.
units.anchor: Do not use AI to create or distribute content that violates copyright or intellectual property

units.why: Warns AI-generated materials made with university resources 'bear high intellectual property risks'; IP risk statement, P52.
units.anchor: bear high intellectual property risks and could expose the university to liability

units.why: 'Do not use AI to deceive others' including fake news and fabricated messages; a deception prohibition with no fitting type, UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: Do not use AI to deceive others
units.uncovered_note: Prohibition on using AI to deceive others or create false communication.

units.why: 'Do not use AI to alter or fabricate data to support false claims' is a research/data integrity rule; P62 (research and scholarship) is closest.
units.anchor: Do not use AI to alter or fabricate data to support false claims or mislead

units.why: 'Do not use AI for any form of unauthorized surveillance of individuals' is a surveillance prohibition with no fitting type.
units.anchor: Do not use AI for any form of unauthorized surveillance of individuals
units.uncovered_note: Prohibition on using AI for unauthorized surveillance of students, faculty or staff.

units.why: 'Do not use AI to harass, bully, or intimidate' is a conduct prohibition; no type, UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: Do not use AI to harass, bully, or intimidate
units.uncovered_note: Prohibition on using AI to harass, bully, intimidate or generate hate speech.

units.why: 'Do not use AI in a manner that discriminates against individuals' based on protected characteristics; bias/harms concern, P53.
units.anchor: Do not use AI in a manner that discriminates against individuals

units.why: 'Do not use AI in any way that compromises academic integrity' ties AI misuse to the Academic Standards Policy; P36 (unauthorized AI as misconduct).
units.anchor: Do not use AI in any way that compromises academic integrity

units.why: The Academic Standards Policy 'prohibits students from cheating, plagiarism, stealing, and lying'; anchors AI misuse in existing misconduct rules, P36.
units.anchor: prohibits students from cheating, plagiarism, stealing, and lying in academic work

units.why: 'Do not employ AI in research without adhering to ethical guidelines and obtaining necessary approvals'; research rule, P62.
units.anchor: Do not employ AI in research without adhering to ethical guidelines and obtaining necessary approvals

units.why: 'These guidelines shall be reviewed as needed' sets a review cycle; P54.
units.anchor: These guidelines shall be reviewed as needed

units.why: Says guidelines 'aim to encourage the creative and innovative exploration and use of AI tools'; institution-level purpose and stance, P56 rather than P02 as it states framework aim not a use rule.
units.anchor: aim to encourage the creative and innovative exploration and use of AI tools

documents.title: AI Guidelines for Students
documents.summary: Student-facing university guidance that defers to each syllabus, expects acknowledgement of AI use, and calls unauthorized use an academic-standards violation. It also lists beneficial learning uses, uses to avoid, privacy and copyright cautions, and career reasons to learn AI.
documents.stance_why: The page says 'Decisions about individual course-level policies should remain the sole responsibility of course instructors' and tells students to 'follow those policies' in each syllabus; it gives general principles but no default allow or ban, so delegates.

units.why: Describes the student guidelines as a 'framework for helping students understand when and how to responsibly and ethically use generative AI'; scope and purpose, P56.

documents.title: Creating a Successful Syllabus (Generative AI section)
documents.summary: Academic Standards Office guidance for faculty on syllabus content, with a Generative-AI section offering baseline and expanded addenda and a sample no-AI-unless-specified statement from one instructor. It leaves the stance to each course.
documents.stance_why: The page asks faculty to 'identify one or more recommended statements' and says the statement 'may, and likely should, vary depending on the course'; the baseline and expanded addenda only say AI use should follow Academic Standards, so no fixed stance is set and the decision goes to instructors.

documents.title: Honor Code | Department of Computer Science
documents.summary: Computer Science department honor code for all CS-major work. It bars using AI or other tools that generate or correct code or answers unless permission is requested, bars outside help on design and implementation, and requires students to protect their work.
documents.stance_why: The department code bans using 'artificial intelligence, or other tools to complete assignments which can generate, translate, or otherwise create/correct code or answers' while allowing exceptions: 'many types of assistive technology may be permitted, but you must ask permission', so AI is banned unless permitted.

units.why: Applies the code to 'ALL kinds of work for classes in the CS major, including programming projects, written text and reports'; scope definition, P61.
units.anchor: further honor code policies detailed below regarding ALL kinds of work for classes in the

units.why: 'Your instructor may state further policies for his or her class and on individual assignments': instructors add rules, P04.
units.anchor: Your instructor may state further policies for his or her class and on individual assignments

units.why: 'For any area you are unsure about, you must request clarification from your course instructor.' P10.
units.anchor: For any area you are unsure about, you must request clarification from your course instructor

units.why: 'all work handed in for credit is to be the result of individual effort'; own-work rule, P29.
units.anchor: all work handed in for credit is to be the result of individual effort

units.why: 'permission to do something on one assignment, in one class, or by one instructor does not automatically give permission in any other context'; P11.
units.anchor: permission to do something on one assignment, in one class, or by one instructor does

units.anchor: seek assistance from official language documentation

units.why: The core rule: you may not 'use assistive technology, artificial intelligence, or other tools to complete assignments which can generate, translate, or otherwise create/correct code or answers'; P19 (no AI producing submitted code), chosen over P21 because 'generate ... create' leads.

units.anchor: Unless permission to do so is granted by the instructor
